judgments.title: Use Restriction Limited to Phase I Only
judgments.reason: The limitation to a Phase I trial is express and narrow but not ambiguous or inconsistent.

judgments.title: Spelling error in are
judgments.reason: “Ere” is plainly intended as “are” in context and does not change the provision's meaning.

judgments.title: Spelling error in use
judgments.reason: “Uae” is readily understood as “use” and does not affect the permitted-use restriction.

judgments.title: Spelling errors in GMP clause
judgments.reason: The corrupted technical phrase “appilcation in ex viva aurologcus” mechanically obscures the precise clinical application authorized by the clause.

judgments.title: Spelling error in quantities
judgments.reason: “QUantitles” is an obvious misspelling of “quantities” that does not alter the requirement.

judgments.title: Spelling error in not
judgments.reason: “Net” is a valid but unintended word substituted for “not,” and if read literally it changes or destroys the prohibition.

judgments.title: Missing space in sent to
judgments.reason: The missing space in “sentto” does not obscure the intended phrase “sent to.”

judgments.title: Missing space in another institution
judgments.reason: “Anotherinstitution” remains readily understandable as “another institution” and does not alter the restriction.

judgments.title: Spelling error in obligations
judgments.reason: “Obligatons” is plainly “obligations” and does not change the provision's meaning.

pos3.clause_name: Paragraph 5 — Ownership, patent applications and commercialization (2007 MTA)
pos3.label: POSITIVE

judgments.title: Require Prior Written Consent Before Patent Filing
judgments.reason: The clause clearly requires contact rather than prior consent; the issue seeks a stronger substantive protection, not construction of the existing text.

judgments.title: Weak IP Ownership Determination Mechanism
judgments.reason: The absence of an agreement mechanism, dispute procedure, or sanction is a negotiation concern rather than an ambiguity or internal inconsistency.

judgments.title: Publication Review Period Lacks Patent Filing Extension
judgments.reason: The provision clearly supplies a 30-day review period and no patent-filing extension; adding one is a negotiated enhancement.

judgments.title: No Right to Remove Proprietary Information from Publications
judgments.reason: The term “review” does not clearly establish whether St. Jude may merely comment or may require redaction, so the practical scope of that right may require construction.

judgments.title: Spelling errors
judgments.reason: The substitution of “2” for “a” in “commercializes 2 product” is a mechanical error that facially affects the quantity and grammar of the trigger.

judgments.title: Spelling error
judgments.reason: “Whieh” is an obvious misspelling of “which” that does not change the clause's meaning.

judgments.title: Overly Broad "But For" Ownership Reach-Through
judgments.reason: The “but for” formulation states a recognizable causation test; the complaint is that its reach is commercially broad, not that it has competing textual meanings.

judgments.title: Unlimited Pre-Publication Review with No Constraint on St. Jude
judgments.reason: The word “review” is unclear as to whether it permits only inspection and comment or also confers authority to demand redaction or delay publication.

judgments.title: Spelling error in patent
judgments.reason: “Pateet” is plainly intended to mean “patent” and does not itself create a construction issue.

judgments.title: Corrupted text in ownership
judgments.reason: The corrupted text “c ■wnership” mechanically obscures the operative subject—St. Jude's ownership interests.

judgments.title: Spelling error in Recipient
judgments.reason: “Rectpient” is an obvious misspelling of the defined party name and creates no competing referent.

judgments.title: Spelling error in Materials
judgments.reason: “Materiele” is readily understood as the defined “Materials” and does not alter the publication obligation.

judgments.title: Spelling errors in review clause
judgments.reason: The severely corrupted phrase “revieW et...1th publiottion” obscures what St. Jude is entitled to review and therefore affects the operative review right.

judgments.title: Spelling error in information
judgments.reason: “Infonnation” is an obvious misspelling of “information” and does not affect scope.
